title: Which of these two is actually better

slides.headline: Two boxes. Same price. //[[gold]]No idea which one.[[/gold]]
slides.sub: You've been stood here for ninety seconds.

slides.headline: The numbers aren't comparable on purpose
slides.body: One's per 100g, one's per serving, and the serving is a size nobody eats. That isn't an accident.

slides.headline: Hold both up and say what you care about
slides.body: Salt. Sugar. Protein. Price per unit. Whatever it actually is — it compares on that, not on a generic score.

turns.text: Which of these has less sugar, really?
The left one looks lower, but that's per 30g and the other's per 45g. Evened out, the right one's lower — 9g against 11.

slides.headline: "Add the other one to the list"
slides.body: And it's still on the list tomorrow, and the week after. You don't lose it the moment you close the app.

slides.headline: It won't recommend the one you can't eat
slides.body: Tell it once about the allergy or the diet. From then on that's part of every comparison, without you saying it again.

slides.headline: Take it to the shop this week
slides.body: Free on iPhone, no sign-up, and you can delete everything in one tap.
